snippet.title: Bolo by Dongleware (MS-DOS, 1994) Gameplay first ten levels
snippet.description:
Bolo is a MS-DOS and Macintosh game by Dongleware, released on CD-ROM in 1994 in Germany. It is a highly innovative brick-breaking game in which the player can move the paddle quite freely around on the screen. The paddle movement is limited only because it cannot move through bricks. In later levels, there are also deadly bricks that destroy the paddle on contact.

The game is full of creative gameplay elements and physics effects, such as varying gravity, rubber bands, magnets, switches, bumpers, varying paddle shapes, changing friction, extra powers and many more. 

There are fifty levels of increasing difficulty. It is possible to save the game and continue later, but the save game is deleted as soon as it is loaded again. This permadeath makes the game quite challenging. 

To increase replay value, many levels have several slightly different versions stored on disc which are chosen randomly during each game. For example some levels will have square shape bricks on one playthrough and round bricks on the next.

A meditative CD quality soundtrack complements the gameplay.

Played on Dosbox 0.74 on OSX.

Legal download of full game ready to play:
http://www.kultmags.com/games.php?folder=Qm9sbw==

More info on the game:
http://www.mobygames.com/game/dos/bolo___/release-info

A level editor programmed by z42:
http://boledit.sourceforge.net/

German review of the game in PowerPlay:
http://www.kultboy.com/index.php?site=t&id=1700

German Dongleware shrine site:
http://www.successdenied.com/dongleware-museum/#bolo1995

Playlist of all my english Let's Plays:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLYy2LvKm9r5gI60isu7xZozg83bQjoSen
